races.name: Randox Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cap Bernat
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 442-day absence for Robin McNeilly under Danny Mullins, this 13-year-old holds Good-ground form from previous seasons and adopts a prominent style that keeps him in contention, though fitness after such a long layoff must be the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Eben Zaabeel
runners_data.note: A J Martin has run him six times in the last 14 days suggesting a yard in form, and while this five-year-old's recent hurdle form on Good and Soft shows finishes outside the frame, his true racing character is that of a hold-up horse — making him dependent on a pace scenario that this race shape is unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: Euro Agent
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends this five-year-old out fresh after 78 days, and he showed a second-place finish on Good ground earlier in his career; however, his natural instinct to race from the rear means the uncontested lead Fox Walk will enjoy is unlikely to produce the end-to-end gallop he needs to deliver a telling late run.

runners_data.name: Fairy Meadow
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's nine-year-old has a worrying tendency to fade in the finish — confirmed by the flag — and with only two runs in the book (one fall, one distant finish), her hold-up style leaves her reliant on stamina that has not yet been demonstrated convincingly over this sort of distance on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Fox Walk
runners_data.note: Noel Kelly's five-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field, and his recent third-to-first profile (5P3-13) on Good ground over similar trips suggests he is arriving in good order 25 days after his last run, giving him every chance to control this race entirely on his own terms under Simon Torrens.

runners_data.name: Mr Caulfield
runners_data.note: Shares his trainer Noel Kelly with Fox Walk, which makes stable tactics an interesting subplot, and his runner-up finish on Good ground over similar distances marks him out as the horse most likely to travel smoothly just off the leader's shoulder and deliver a clean challenge in the straight.

runners_data.name: Tullynakill
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount on this unknown quantity for S R B Crawford — no days-since-last-run figure, no form string, and an unknown going profile make this a true wildcard, but Slevin's presence at least ensures the horse will be placed intelligently in the race regardless of its unexposed profile.

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Thomas McGettigan's six-year-old arrives 12 days fresh, but a form string of 08 and a consistent history of finishing eighth or worse across all her starts — including on Good ground — combined with the fades-in-finish flag makes a meaningful contribution here difficult to envisage even in a small, weak maiden.

runners_data.name: Greenroad Girl
runners_data.note: A four-year-old for R K Watson with Darragh O'Keeffe booked, she has placed in two runs on Good ground over similar distances but carries the lightest weight in the field at 156lbs; her hold-up style will not be ideally suited to the likely race shape but her youth and lighter burden give her an outside residual chance if the pace is stronger than expected.

races.paceDynamic: Fox Walk is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, will dictate a sustainable gallop from the outset on Good ground at Downpatrick over 2m2f. The redistribution of Fairy Meadow, Eben Zaabeel, and Euro Agent to midfield on the map reflects the reality that all three are true hold-up types who will be tracking from behind rather than pressing Fox Walk — meaning the pace-setter faces no pressure and can control tempo entirely on its own terms. This creates a classic lone-leader scenario: a measured, front-end gallop that stretches the field out without punishing the leader, making it very difficult for deep hold-up horses to generate the momentum to close late. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically be covered in the race map, with Fox Walk almost certain to secure the lead uncontested and Mr Caulfield and Cap Bernat the most likely to lock in prominent positions behind; this race shape strongly favours a prominent or lead-tracking profile that can travel close to Fox Walk and pounce before the hold-up brigade have time to wind up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fox Walk Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fox Walk leads without pressure and sets a steady-to-fair gallop throughout, dictating the race from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Fox Walk can dictate every yard on his own terms, and horses close enough to track him — namely Mr Caulfield and Cap Bernat — will be ideally positioned to challenge turning in without expending unnecessary energy. True hold-up types at the rear will be left with too much ground to make up on a runner who has never had to over-exert himself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Fox Walk's early lead causes one of the prominent trackers to travel strongly throughout and overpower him at the final flight.
scenarios.body: Mr Caulfield, who has course-related Good-ground form and a second-place finish to his name, is best placed to sit a length off Fox Walk and produce a clean challenge in the straight. Cap Bernat, despite his lengthy absence at 442 days off, has shown he handles this sort of Good ground and could outfinish the leader if his fitness is sharp.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually honest and gaps appear late, allowing a well-held hold-up runner to pick off tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Euro Agent, trained by Gordon Elliott and with Good-ground form in his recent history, is the most likely beneficiary if the race develops a strong enough gallop to bring a closer into play, though his redistribution tag means this is not his natural scenario to exploit. Eben Zaabeel has similar going credentials but must overcome the same limitation of racing further back than his style suits in a field with limited genuine pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race and the field thins dramatically, gifting the race to whoever survives cleanly.
scenarios.body: With Fairy Meadow already carrying a fades-in-finish flag and Nelliestar showing a consistent pattern of poor finishes, attrition could reshuffle the order entirely, leaving Greenroad Girl or Tullynakill — both lightly raced types with unknowns in their profiles — to benefit. Tullynakill in particular is an unexposed five-year-old with an unknown going profile, meaning a messy race that negates stamina or style advantages could suit a fresh runner under J J Slevin.

watchPoints.text: Fox Walk must be monitored at every hurdle — if he jumps poorly or makes an early mistake, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes wide open for Mr Caulfield to inherit the lead.
Mr Caulfield and Fox Walk are trained by the same handler, Noel C Kelly; watch for any signs of stable pacemaking tactics where Fox Walk sets it up deliberately for Mr Caulfield to come through.

Fairy Meadow's tendency to fade in the finish, combined with being raced out of her natural hold-up position, creates a jumping risk mid-race — her presence in midfield could cause interference if she weakens abruptly approaching the final flight.

Tullynakill is completely unexposed under J J Slevin with no days-since-last-run recorded and no form to assess — if she shows any natural class, she could outrun a big price in a weak nine-runner maiden field.

Eben Zaabeel's trainer A J Martin recorded six runs in the last 14 days — watch if the horse drifts or shortens in the market, as yard form could be a significant hidden factor that the bare form line of a single 0 run this season does not reflect.

races.name: WillWeGo.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and clear pace-maker; Danny Mullins likely to slot straight to the front and control this from flag to finish; Good ground suits (5 from 7 similar-going runs in the frame); drop back from 18f trips looks fine at 2m2f; 168lbs is a burden but unchallenged pace is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for J J Slevin and John Patrick Ryan; trainer has 0 wins from 14 in 14 days so no hot form wave here; Good ground specialist (14 from 14 similar-going runs including a win and three placings); placed at 17f and 18f suggesting this 2m2f trip is within range; needs Ripsnorter to set a strong enough gallop to reel in.

runners_data.name: Youknowthecode
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard in 14-day form (1/39 — low strike rate); hold-up performer with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish; only one run in similar Good going from four tries; recent form string of 860-0 is uninspiring and the fade flag is a concern at the business end of this trip.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type at nine years old for John Joseph Hanlon; Harry Sexton claims 7lb which is a meaningful allowance; has finished fifth in four of his last five comparable Good-ground runs — consistent but not a winner; tongue strap fitted, Good ground is his element (14/15 sim-going runs), but inability to win is a recurring theme.

runners_data.name: South Of Killerig
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer whose true racing style puts him closer to the front than his mapped midfield slot reflects; in a race dominated by hold-up types, he could work his way forward, but the field's density makes it hard to secure his preferred position; six from eight Good-ground runs places him in the frame without winning, and STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Echinacea
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Simon Torrens and Noel C Kelly; 64 days off the track is the longest absence in the field and fitness is a genuine query; two placings from five similar-going runs include second-place finishes; Good ground is acceptable and the 4yo allowance is modest but the layoff is a flag to watch.

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Has won at 17f on Good for Stuart Curling, but the fade-in-finish flag and the fact he is a true hold-up horse pushed into a nominal midfield position both limit his chance in a race shape this controlled; STYLE_FIT of 0.91 means discounting him in scenarios where he needs to be further back than traffic allows; 158lbs is a modest weight.

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a legitimate place profile; two wins from 14 at 22f on Good and a recent third (155lbs is lowest weighted prominent type in the field); Mr B T Stone claims 7lb, a useful allowance for a trainer with no recent 14-day runners; course-distance experience and Good ground are genuine assets here.

runners_data.name: Banphrionsa Alainn
runners_data.note: Lowest-class hold-up filly in the field (OR 78); carries a fade-in-finish warning; only three comparable runs in sim-going suggest limited evidence at this level; the redistribution out of her natural hold-up slot into midfield compounds the task, and the 7lb claim from Dylan O'Connor is the headline angle on a filly with modest form.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a blinkers/tongue strap combination; form reads U4-300 with no wins in nine Good-ground runs from the mapping data; the fade flag adds to concerns; naturally suited to racing off the pace but with so many of the same ilk in this field, getting a clean run late will be competitive — STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reinforces tempered expectations.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type for Adrian McGuinness (3 wins from 21 in 14 days — modest but active); placed three times from nine Good-ground runs; ran just 12 days ago; Darragh O'Keeffe is a quality booking and Granlahan's recent form (3-U-3-6-2-4) shows some consistency at this level; displaced from natural rear position, but less likely to be stranded than some others here.

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 74) with a fade-in-finish flag and consistent tail-end form (10th, 6th, 11th, 13th, 11th in recent runs); naturally a hold-up type redistributed to midfield; claimed by Conor Clarke 7lb but the booking cannot disguise weak underlying form; Good ground is acceptable but the handicap mark and recent record offer little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap hurdle and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge him, Danny Mullins can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground at Downpatrick. The bulk of the field are hold-up or midfield types, meaning Ripsnorter faces no meaningful early pressure and can set a rhythm entirely on his own terms. South Of Killerig, He Who Dares, Granlahan, Banphrionsa Alainn, Firstupbestdressed, and John Dixen are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions because there is simply no room at the rear for so many alike, and of these, Granlahan and He Who Dares are best-credentialled to secure a forward slot. This race shape — a lone front-runner controlling pace on a flat, right-handed track — strongly favours that front-runner or an organised prominent-tracking horse who can settle within striking range and pounce at the second-last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Controls And Scores
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable gallop and quickens out of the last.
scenarios.body: Mullins can set his own fractions, save ground throughout, and present at the final flight with a clear lead; on Good ground Ripsnorter has finished in front within the last five runs at this trip and this style benefits most when pace is owned from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a settled prominent or midfield horse travels smoothly in Ripsnorter's slipstream and produces a clean jump at the last to collar him.
scenarios.body: Le Diablo or Menas Miracle, both operating on suitable Good ground, are capable of sitting a length or two off the pace and finding extra when asked; Menas Miracle has two course-distance wins at 22f on Good and Slevin on Le Diablo has the class to exploit a carbon-copy gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter fades badly from three out having gone too hard early, opening the race to a late rush from the midfield cluster.
scenarios.body: Pahlavi or Echinacea, the most consistent hold-up performers on Good ground in the field, would be the primary beneficiaries as the pace evaporates; however, several of the nominal midfield runners are true hold-up types displaced forward, so the closing kick will be muddied and no single closer has a commanding profile here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Contested Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If South Of Killerig or He Who Dares push forward to challenge Ripsnorter early, creating an unexpectedly honest pace.
scenarios.body: A contested early fractions race on Good ground would compress finishing positions and open the door for a fresh horse with tactical speed to win out of the chasing pack; Granlahan has placed in three of eleven Good-ground runs and with Darragh O'Keeffe retains each-way claims if the race is run to suit.

watchPoints.text: Ripsnorter's early behaviour is the pivot of the entire race — if Mullins is forced to go faster than intended by any challenger pushing up, his stamina at 168lbs over 2m2f becomes a live concern.
Le Diablo has J J Slevin aboard and is a genuine each-way threat if the pace is even and he can travel smoothly, but John Patrick Ryan's 14-day record of 0/14 is worth noting as a trainer form flag.

Menas Miracle is the only prominent-style horse with a realistic chance of tracking Ripsnorter at close quarters; Mr B T Stone's 7lb claim helps the weight, and two course-distance wins on Good make this worth watching from the front of the chasing pack.

Several hold-up horses — Granlahan, He Who Dares, South Of Killerig — may push forward out of their natural role in the first mile, and any mid-race traffic incident or bunching at hurdles could affect the genuine closers Pahlavi and Echinacea late on.

Echinacea's 64-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; if she is short of peak fitness, her hold-up style means she will not get competitive until the final two hurdles — watch whether she is warming up fluently in the pre-race canter.

races.name: North Down Marquees Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tribal Moon
runners_data.note: Consistent enough on Good ground with a third in similar conditions, but a natural hold-up horse whose true style is compromised in a field loaded with rear-runners; Conor Stone-Walsh takes over for Noel Kelly and the tongue-tie is applied, though the redistribution to midfield limits its chance.|

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with Kevin Healy (7) aboard for Cian Collins; hold prominent position naturally and has shown placing form consistently on Good ground, including a second over 19f — the step to 2m6f looks workable and this is a horse whose profile slots neatly into the expected race shape.|

runners_data.name: Fortis Et Liber
runners_data.note: The lone front runner and key pace-setter for Colin Bowe; only two starts but Good-ground form reads fine, and Ricky Doyle takes the ride — the style-fit tag reflects it being mapped slightly out of position given its confirmed lead role, but it is uncontested up front and that is a genuine advantage over 2m6f.|

runners_data.name: Fuusland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old has ability suggested by its OR of 120 but has only raced twice and Danny Gilligan inherits a hold-up specialist who cannot easily get to the rear in this crowded field — shuffled into midfield on the map, its chance hinges on a perfect run materialising from an unnatural position.|

runners_data.name: Majestic Horizon
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed, with two thirds on Good ground for PJ Rothwell; Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant booking, the unknown style adds intrigue, and 101 days off means freshness, though it must prove it stays 2m6f.|

runners_data.name: Salty Racer
runners_data.note: Flagged as a hold-up type that fades in the finish — a worrying combination at 2m6f on a stiff track; Simon Torrens rides for Noel Kelly and the sole run on Good ground was an eighth, so there is little evidence to build a case.|

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: Form reads PPP/PU in recent starts and the OR of 80 is the lowest in the field; a genuine hold-up horse unable to settle at the rear due to field composition, and the visor first time alongside a seven-day turnaround for a small trainer makes this a very difficult horse to side with.|

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for PJ Rothwell but has been placed nowhere in four runs on Good ground and is flagged as a fader; Tiernan Power Roche takes the ride and the 12-day turnaround is fine, but the profile of a horse who cannot get competitive when it counts is a concern at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Six Mile Suzy
runners_data.note: 223 days off the track is a significant concern, and the form on Good ground shows a 15th and a 12th; Shane O'Callaghan (3) rides for a trainer with no runners in the past 14 days — the tongue-tie is present but there is very little here to inspire confidence on return from a lengthy absence.|

runners_data.name: Ritz Plan
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a strong booking for a four-year-old carrying top weight for its age; Ritz Plan has solid placed form but its one run on Good going produced a seventh — the handicap marks of seconds and fourths have come on Heavy or yielding, so the Good surface is the key unknown to resolve.|

races.paceDynamic: Fortis Et Liber is the sole confirmed front runner and will lead from the off over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Downpatrick, with no rival likely to seriously contest that position early — the pace will therefore be controlled and sustainable rather than pressurised. Coded Welder and Ritz Plan are the genuine prominent types who will track in second and third, keeping Fortis Et Liber honest without forcing a war, which sets up a steadily-run race likely to favour those travelling well close to the pace into the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear — Tribal Moon, Fuusland, and Tommy Go Maith are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many of them to fill natural rear positions, meaning their ability to execute their preferred style is compromised. This race shape — a controlled lone leader, a genuine pace to chase but not a scorching one — clearly favours the prominent and tracking profiles, with horses able to sit just off Fortis Et Liber and pounce from the second-last flight best placed to exploit the steady tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fortis Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Fortis Et Liber sets a steady, uncontested lead and the race is decided by who travels best close to the pace into the home straight.
scenarios.body: Fortis Et Liber dictates a comfortable tempo and the race becomes a sustained stamina test from the second-last, suiting horses tracking in the top three who can pick off the leader late. Coded Welder and Ritz Plan, as genuine prominent runners with sound form at this trip on Good ground, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fortis Wins Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Fortis Et Liber's controlled pace is slow enough that its stamina reserves are never truly tested and it simply outstays a flat field.
scenarios.body: Having set a frugal gallop, Fortis Et Liber reaches the final hurdle full of running and the chasers find the margin already too great to close. Its Good-ground form is solid for a five-year-old at this early career stage and Colin Bowe's runner could prove better than its limited form suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage to finish strongly from the back of midfield.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Tribal Moon or Fuusland — both true hold-up horses — to navigate a clear route through a tiring field in the closing stages, which is structurally less likely given they are racing out of their natural position and cannot guarantee a clean run. Fuusland has the Gordon Elliott backing and decent form on Good ground, giving it the best residual chance among the back-markers if everything goes right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is misjudged or the field bunches badly, turning the race into a scramble from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A disorganised race with no clear tempo could produce an unexpected winner from anywhere in the field, but horses with stamina warnings — Salty Racer, Jolly D'olivate, Six Mile Suzy, all flagged as fades in finish — are the least likely to benefit. Majestic Horizon, lightly raced and unexposed, retains the most residual upside among the wildcards if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Fortis Et Liber's lead control is the pivot of the entire race — if Ricky Doyle goes too slowly, the field bunches and prominent horses like Coded Welder pounce before the last; if he goes too fast, the race opens up for anything still travelling.|

Fuusland and Tribal Moon are true hold-up horses forced into midfield — watch whether Danny Gilligan and Conor Stone-Walsh can find any daylight in the straight, as a traffic jam among the redistributed back-markers could produce a chaotic finish.|

J J Slevin's booking on Ritz Plan at 4 years old deserves respect — if the Good ground is no issue for the youngster, it could be travelling much better than its opponents into the home straight despite going form question marks.|

Majestic Horizon's unexposed profile and 101-day layoff make it one to monitor in the paddock and early in the race — Darragh O'Keeffe riding a lightly-raced unknown for Rothwell could mean it is better than its placed-only form currently shows.|

Six Mile Suzy returning from 223 days off is a significant stability flag for the entire field — if it jumps poorly or interferes early, the compact field at a tight track like Downpatrick could create problems for those at the back of midfield.|

races.name: AJC Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form includes a win at 19f on Good (25 days ago) and a tendency to fade late, making this 2m6f stamina test a concern; A J Martin's yard is cold (0/6 in 14 days) and the horse's finishing record invites caution.

runners_data.name: Kashchei
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on Good going and ran well on similar surfaces (8/13 in sim-going), but 62 days off the track for a yard running 0/13 in the last fortnight is a flag; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim could help but the layoff is the chief worry.

runners_data.name: Cozone
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with proven stamina (won over 22f on Soft, placed on Good) and a patient handler in Matthew J Smith, though 79 days off the track is a concern; shaped to suit a searching gallop but will need the field to come back to him.

runners_data.name: Shinnhill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won over 18f on Good going and is in very sharp order (22 days since last run, 1W2P in sim-going); natural position just off the pace is ideal in this shape and Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim is a useful allowance.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Strong Gavin Cromwell runner, 5/35 in 14 days showing the yard is firing; ran five consecutive Good-ground races and placed in four, travels prominently, and the recent win over 20f on Good is exactly the profile to exploit an uncontested pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's runner is a genuine hold-up specialist with four second-place finishes in recent runs — but the crowded rear forces him into a midfield role here; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92, his chance is tempered by operating outside his natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on Good going and has solid sim-going figures (6/6), but as a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the redistribution, Sean Flanagan will need to manage his position carefully to avoid being caught in traffic; the style compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a strong Good-ground profile (13/15, 2 wins) including a recent win over 26f — exactly today's trip — and Gordon Elliott's stable has won 1/39 in the last fortnight suggesting quiet but functional; blinkers on, age nine, but jumping accuracy is the key to how long he lasts.

runners_data.name: Tell Nobody Nothin
runners_data.note: 107-day absence is a significant concern for Noel Meade's prominent racer, even though the win came over 20f on Good and the form string includes several placed efforts at today's distance; Joshua Halford's 7lb claim helps but the layoff makes him an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a win over 18f and placed multiple times on Good going, but a natural hold-up style is displaced into midfield here under the redistribution; Donagh Meyler is competent, yet the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects the structural disadvantage of not racing where he's most effective.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner (OR 87) in the field with recent form reading 143040, suggesting inconsistency; prominent style is natural but class is the limiting factor over this trip and Daniel King faces a stiff task against rivals rated 15-23lb superior.

races.paceDynamic: Down Around is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, will stride into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset over this 2m6f trip on Good ground. Seven Towers, Shinnhill, and Tell Nobody Nothin are the natural prominent types who will track behind at a respectful distance, creating a well-strung-out field rather than a bunched scrimmage. The absence of pace pressure means the fractions will likely be honest but not searching, preserving the stamina of those who travel fluently in behind — a shape that rewards hold-up horses who have the class to close from a true position, rather than those forced wide or into a false berth. This field carries more hold-up types than the rear can accommodate — Penzance, Tolka Row, and Mickey Cohen are genuine closers but the map pushes them into midfield, meaning Down Around's lead is structurally unchallenged; the race shape therefore most favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and pounce from a natural position in the final circuit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around controls a steady-honest gallop unchallenged and the prominent trackers travel within themselves before striking.
scenarios.body: Down Around sets a sustainable fractions, gifting Seven Towers and Shinnhill a dream sit just off the bridle; with stamina reserves intact, a prominent racer who jumps fluently can pick the leader off from two out without needing a brutal finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and Down Around, jumping accurately, builds an unassailable lead that the hold-up horses cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: Down Around's Good-going record (13 of 15 runs, 2 wins) underlines suitability, and at 2m6f a fresh nine-year-old who jumps well can steal several lengths unnoticed; prominent chasers fail to close the gap from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up rally falls short
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely brisk enough in the middle mile to string the field and allow the true closers to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Kashchei and Bruant have the form profiles to emerge late but their redistribution out of their natural position costs momentum early; at best they pick off tired rivals for a place rather than winning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos/interference plays out
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping error or fall disrupts the front group and reshuffles the order dramatically in the final mile.
scenarios.body: Midfield horses like Penzance or Mickey Cohen — displaced from their natural position yet possessing the raw form — could emerge if the principals are checked or unseated; but this is the least structurally supported outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Down Around's jumping — if he makes an early error the entire race shape collapses, as he is the sole pace-maker and any disruption removes the controlled lead that underpins Scenario A.

Seven Towers is closely monitored: Gavin Cromwell's yard is 5/35 in 14 days (firing) and this horse has placed on Good going five times in a row, making him the standout beneficiary of the dominant shape — market moves deserve attention.

Penzance, Tolka Row, and Mickey Cohen are all genuine closers mapped into midfield due to field congestion at the rear; watch whether any of them drift widest to find a cleaner position, as their actual finishing kick depends on not being boxed in.

Tell Nobody Nothin's 107-day absence is the longest in the field — watch for signs in the paddock and early race movement that Noel Meade has him cherry-ripe, as his natural prominent style suits if fit.

Shinnhill's trainer Neil McKnight has no runners in the 14-day form window (0/0), offering no stable indicator; monitor the horse's jumping — a fluent round at Downpatrick at 22 days fresh could see Finegan's claim prove decisive.

races.name: Cosy Group Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Barton Sky
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's eight-year-old has strong good-going form credentials but is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — in a field where the map has more closers than places at the back, it is likely to race further forward than ideal but still not as prominently as the natural P types; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers its chance unless chaos plays into its hands.

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Gerard O'Leary's seven-year-old has placed three times in similar going but a 0W record from 15 good-going runs raises a stamina or resolution question over this trip; a true hold-up horse whose 0/9 trainer 14-day strike rate gives no added confidence heading in.

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: The McConnell-trained seven-year-old brings two wins from nine good-going starts and holds course form at the right trip, with the tongue-tie applied again; a natural prominent racer who should slot into an ideal stalking position behind Herja and is well-suited by the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Philip Donovan takes the ride on Slattery's eight-year-old who has been remarkably consistent with six places from 15 good-going runs including a win here — a horse who races prominently and stays well, making it a natural beneficiary of a steady pace set by Herja.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: Cromwell's five-year-old has genuine ability having won and placed on good ground but is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield due to the congested rear; the tongue-tie is applied again but its 5/35 trainer 14-day strike rate and out-of-role positioning mean it faces a tougher ask than its OR suggests.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old carries the tongue-strap and brings two wins and a third from good and similar going, racing prominently as is its style; the 41-day break is worth noting but Elliott's horses often return ready, and James Smith's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable — a live contender from the front rank.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Patrick Griffin's six-year-old is the lone front-runner with a strong record of placing from 13 good-going starts and clearly loves the conditions; Harry Sexton (7lb claim) will be able to dictate fully on this track and at this trip, and while Herja is OR 105 versus rivals all on 119-120, controlling the tempo gives it every chance of running well into the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Herja is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the off over this 2m3½f trip at Downpatrick, setting a measured, uncontested pace that is unlikely to be extreme in either direction. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Herja's rider Harry Sexton can dictate fully and control tempo, creating a race that is likely to be run at a steady-to-fair gallop before quickening late — a shape that typically rewards prominent racers who travel close to the pace and pounce at the right moment. Kevin's Pride, Killeemore Lad, and Spinola Bay are the natural prominent types best positioned to exploit this shape, sitting just off Herja in a clean racing position. This field holds more hold-up types than can realistically be placed at the rear — Barton Sky, Jabbar, and Robbies Rock are redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they are genuine hold-up horses who will likely find themselves with ground to make up on the eventual pace collapse that may or may not materialise; the race shape therefore favours the prominent and prominent-to-lead runners who can save ground and strike from a handy position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Herja Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Herja leads unchallenged and the race develops into a steady gallop with a single sustained burst from two out, setting up a clean race for those travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: Herja sets fractions to suit, with Kevin's Pride, Killeemore Lad, and Spinola Bay travelling within striking range and able to challenge on the bridle approaching the final obstacles; the lack of pace pressure means the hold-up horses are unlikely to close enough ground in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Herja Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly modest and Herja is never seriously pressed, stealing the race by running rivals into the ground on the long Downpatrick circuit.
scenarios.body: Herja's OR of 105 flatters a horse with a strong record of placing in good-going races, and at a slow pace it may simply not be caught by hold-up types asked to produce a sustained run over the closing stages; prominent runners who fail to track closely enough are the biggest losers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get Into It
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens sooner than expected in the back straight, stringing out the field and creating gaps for the hold-up types to thread through.
scenarios.body: Robbies Rock and Jabbar have the ability to close on a collapsing pace if the fractions prove uneven, though both are disadvantaged by mapping out of their true position; Spinola Bay's experience at this trip also gives it a window here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the prominent horses early and reshuffle the field, turning this into a more chaotic contest that plays into attrition rather than positional play.
scenarios.body: Beginners' chases at Downpatrick carry inherent jumping risk, and any fallers or loose horses could open the door for a hold-up horse who avoids trouble; Barton Sky's experience and Robbies Rock's prior win form give them claims if the front and prominent ranks make mistakes.

watchPoints.text: Herja — with no pressure expected for the lead, watch whether Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) sets a genuinely contestable gallop or an overly modest one; if the pace is pedestrian, the prominent horses behind may struggle to quicken past rather than around it.

Kevin's Pride and Killeemore Lad — both prominent types targeting the same ground just off Herja, and if they bump or crowd each other early over the novice fences, one or both could lose their rhythm at a critical point in a beginners' chase.

Robbies Rock and Jabbar — genuine hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves stuck in midfield with significant ground to recover; if Herja controls the tempo and there is no sudden pace surge to create a gap, their finishing runs may arrive too late.

Jumping watch across the whole field — this is a beginners' steeplechase and all seven runners are relatively inexperienced over fences; errors at the open ditch or the water jump at Downpatrick could reshuffle the entire race shape regardless of pace scenario.

Spinola Bay — Elliott's horse has the profile of a potential market mover on the day given the strong trainer yard, and if it drifts or shortens sharply in the ring, that is a useful read on confidence from connections heading into an uncertain beginners' contest.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a win and a place on similar good ground at this sort of trip; 34 days off and a U in recent form tempers enthusiasm, but Ross O'Sullivan's runner is capable of finishing well if the pace collapses the field late.

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with outstanding Good-ground credentials (10/11, 1W4P); only 10 days since last run and a 10-year-old, so fitness is not a concern, but must survive the battle with Annarubyrose to fulfil his role.

runners_data.name: Kalsman
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent racer with two wins on Good and a strong recent record (11/15 similar going); last win was over 20f so the 2m3½f trip is fine, and sitting just off a contested lead suits his profile perfectly.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with three consecutive top-four finishes on good ground; the 21-day break is fine, and Daniel King takes over in the saddle — best watched to see if the pace suits him sweeping through late.

runners_data.name: Full Noise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who handles Good ground adequately (8/15) and has shown consistency at this level; the amateur rider Mr D McGill claims 7lbs which helps offset the weight, and a place in the slipstream of the leaders suits his running style.

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a significant concern over this trip if the pace is strong; 45 days off and a recent run of poor form (F0-96) makes this a tough ask even on suitable ground.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has hit the frame twice in 15 similar-going runs but is yet to win on Good; Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking and the horse is lightly enough weighted at 158lbs to be competitive if he gets a clean round of jumping.

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: The best course-and-going profile in the field (12/15 similar going, 3W7P) and ran well just 10 days ago; Conor Stone-Walsh partners a horse who clearly loves this type of test, and his hold-up style is genuine rather than enforced by the map.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse squeezed into midfield on the map because the rear is congested; form figures of P and P on recent runs and only one place from 14 similar-going starts mean the handicap mark of 85 is hard to exploit from whatever position he settles.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Shaped well when winning over 22f on Good recently, and J J Slevin is an excellent booking; hold-up style is genuine and the five-year-old has scope, but the string of pulled-up runs before that win invites caution.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has struggled to land a blow in six recent starts (best a third over 20f); the ground and trip are fine but a career mark of 84 and a run of 0-3667 suggests this handicap mark still finds him out.

runners_data.name: The Cobblers Wife
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good last time and Danny Mullins keeps the ride, so the form is live; however, she is a natural hold-up mare who finds herself mapped to a more prominent slot because the rear of the field is over-subscribed, and her best chance depends on getting a clear passage late rather than pressing the pace.

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old whose natural closing style is compromised by the congested hold-up contingent; only 3/15 runs on similar going have produced a placed finish and he needs everything to go right from an awkward position.

runners_data.name: Nobody
runners_data.note: Five-year-old flagged as a fader in the finish with no wins or places in 15 similar-going starts; genuine hold-up type who is racing out of his natural map position given the volume of closers, and the overall profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Baltinglass Hill
runners_data.note: 110 days off is a significant freshness concern even for a Rothwell yard that posts a strong 3/19 strike-rate over 14 days; P J Rothwell's recent form gives some trainer angle, but 16 starts on similar going without a win (0W2P) tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who must battle Gorthill for the lead from the off; her record of 9/9 on similar going shows she handles conditions, but five-year-olds taking on a hardened front-runner in a duel over 2m3½f often find the contest too demanding in the closing stages.

races.paceDynamic: Gorthill and Annarubyrose are confirmed front-runners who will go head-to-head from the off over 2m3½f on good ground at Downpatrick, creating a genuinely contested gallop that is unlikely to ease at any stage. With both horses committed to the lead, the pace will be honest and sustained, placing a premium on jumping accuracy and the ability to travel comfortably in behind without burning stamina early. This race shape — two genuine pace-setters fighting for supremacy — historically benefits prominent and mid-division horses who can sit just off the heat and pounce in the straight, rather than true front-runners who must absorb the duel or hold-up horses who will have too much ground to make up on a fair gallop. The field also holds more genuine hold-up types (My Policy, The Cobblers Wife, Deadheat, Nobody) than the rear of the field can accommodate, meaning Kalsman, Full Noise, My Cullen and King's Son are best placed to exploit their naturally prominent position just behind the two leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gorthill and Annarubyrose burn each other up and a prominent tracker pounces between the last two fences.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel between the two front-runners sets an honest gallop that gradually saps their reserves, and a horse racing comfortably in third or fourth makes smooth headway from three out to win going away; Kalsman's strong Good-ground record (11/15 similar going, two wins) and Our Zebo's course-seasoned profile make them the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacesetter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Annarubyrose or Gorthill drops away early and one front-runner controls a more measured pace to steal the race.
scenarios.body: A single leader dictating a less frenetic tempo sets a comfortable gallop that turns the race into a test of jumping and class rather than pure stamina, allowing the leader to conserve enough for a genuine finish; Gorthill's excellent Good-ground record (10/11 similar going) and experience at this trip makes this the more likely front-runner to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses the front-runners and a horse from fifth or sixth sweeps through in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A fast, contested gallop that fully destroys the leading pair opens the door for a horse racing smoothly in mid-division to pick off the weakening leaders from two out; Run For The Border (three recent top-four finishes on good ground) and Driveonwill (won over this trip and going) hold the best profiles for this shape, though ground covered early limits the margin.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that the entire field strings out and genuine hold-up horses mount a late challenge from the rear.
scenarios.body: This shape requires My Policy, The Cobblers Wife, or Deadheat to overcome their redistributed starting positions and find clear daylight at the critical stage, making it the least likely outcome given those horses are racing out of their natural role; Our Zebo, who handles this track well (12/15 similar going), is the closest to a genuine hold-up horse with a realistic late claim.

watchPoints.text: Gorthill and Annarubyrose will fight for the lead from flag fall — watch if either capitulates before halfway, as that fundamentally changes the pace shape and who benefits.

Kalsman sat prominently in three of his last five Good-ground starts and finished in the first three each time — watch him travelling into contention from three out as the prime prominent-racer threat.

Our Zebo's 12/15 course-and-going profile is the standout statistical angle in the field — watch whether Conor Stone-Walsh can get him into a race-winning position from his hold-up berth given the volume of horses ahead of him.

Wing Back's flag for fading in the finish combined with 45 days off and a recent run of 6-9-13-U-3 makes him a jumping risk at a track where accurate fencing is essential — watch his jumping from the fourth fence onwards.

Not So Serious with J J Slevin is worth monitoring at the early stages — if Slevin pushes forward to secure a prominent pitch rather than dropping the five-year-old in, the horse's profile improves markedly given recent winning form over this trip and going.

races.name: Downpatrick Racecourse Style Awards Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with six runs on good ground returning strong sim-going figures (14/15), and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim helps offset the 167lb burden; races from the rear in his natural role and will need a strong pace from Finnians Row to set him alight over this 2m2f trip.

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 19f on good ground and his sim-going record (11/15) reads well for today; Kevin Sexton partners a horse whose authentic hold-up style is correctly mapped, though a step back in trip from his recent win is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Cromwell's seven-year-old has been lightly raced recently (58 days off) and his form shows a run of unplaced efforts; by nature a genuine come-from-behind type, he is placed in midfield on the map only because the hold-up berths are full — his actual position in running is likely further back, which tempers his prospects in this particular race shape.

runners_data.name: Finnians Row
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 2m on good ground make him the standout pace angle, and McLoughlin's booking of apprentice Niall Moore keeps the weight at 153lbs; as the lone front-runner against a field of closers, he holds a significant tactical edge if he can control the tempo without being tested.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: A five-year-old lightly weighted at 150lbs with a modest sim-going record (5/13), and while his last two runs showed minor improvement, he is a genuine hold-up horse whose midfield map placement reflects field congestion at the rear rather than his true running style — discount him in any scenario that requires a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: His second last time out over 16f on good ground is encouraging and Phillip Enright is a shrewd booking, but this ten-year-old's natural place is at the back of the field; like Piccolo Player and Stuntman Steve, he has been placed in midfield on the map purely by redistribution, and his chance is curtailed in a shape that offers so little pace for closers to aim at.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Three wins from recent starts on good ground and correctly mapped as a genuine prominent racer — the one horse who can legitimately sit behind Finnians Row and have first use of his finishing effort; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is a significant advantage on 147lbs over this 2m2f trip.

races.paceDynamic: Finnians Row is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, will dictate terms at whatever tempo suits Niall Moore from the outset. Rightfolksplease is the only genuine prominent-type in the field and will sit just behind, giving Finnians Row a soft lead rather than any meaningful pressure. The bulk of the field — War Correspondent, Beggars Rock, Stuntman Steve, Piccolo Player, and Presenting Lad — are all natural hold-up horses, meaning the real race unfolds in the final circuit as closers attempt to reel in what could be a well-conserved front-runner. This field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Stuntman Steve, Piccolo Player, and Presenting Lad are genuine come-from-behind horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map but are unlikely to secure even that position naturally given their true style. The race shape strongly favours either Finnians Row to control and convert from the front, or the two most class-laden hold-up horses — War Correspondent and Beggars Rock — who are authentic in their position and have the form on good ground to run on late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Finnians Row Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Finnians Row bowls along in front at a measured gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Finnians Row has won his last two outings over 2m on good ground and faces no genuine pace rivals here, allowing McLoughlin's ten-year-old to dictate a sustainable tempo and sprint clear from the last; with Rightfolksplease likely tracking in second, the front two could have first run on all rivals turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Duo Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Finnians Row sets a genuine clip and the closers have enough ground to make up in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: War Correspondent and Beggars Rock are both proven on good ground and racing in their true roles with authentic finishing kicks; a strong pace from Finnians Row gives these two a target to chase, and either could sweep past the tiring leader approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rightfolksplease Presses Through
scenarios.trigger: If Rightfolksplease tracks Finnians Row closely, applies pressure from the second-last, and the front-runner weakens.
scenarios.body: Rightfolksplease has won three of his last five runs on good ground over this trip and carries only 147lbs, giving Kevin Healy a live chance if he can collar Finnians Row when it matters; his genuine prominent style means he is correctly placed on the map and can capitalise if the leader over-extends early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and Stuntman Steve, Piccolo Player, or Presenting Lad manage to secure a closer position than their natural style dictates.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on these three racing out of role and is materially discounted because they are true hold-up types whose style fit scores flag concern; even if conditions conspire, their redistribution to midfield on the map overstates how close they will actually be.

watchPoints.text: Finnians Row — watch whether Niall Moore elects to dawdle or force a genuine gallop; if he is allowed to steal a march from the front without any pressure from Rightfolksplease, the closers may be left with too much to do from the second-last.

Rightfolksplease — monitor how aggressively Kevin Healy tracks Finnians Row; if he sits too far off the pace, he surrenders his positional advantage, but if he presses too soon he risks flattening out before the last.

War Correspondent — Harry Sexton's 7lb claim is attractive but the 167lb weight is the heaviest in the field; watch whether that burden blunts the finishing kick that his hold-up style depends upon over this trip.

Stuntman Steve, Piccolo Player, Presenting Lad — all three are natural hold-up horses crowded into a field already dominated by closers; if any of them attempt to race closer to the pace than their style dictates, it could disrupt the midfield order and cost them energy they need for the run-in.

Beggars Rock — dropped back from 24f to 19f last time and won, now dropping to 18f; worth watching whether the shorter trip proves sharp enough for a horse whose best recent form has come over further ground.
